title: O2 + PtF6 -> O2+[PtF6]- : bond order of the dioxygenyl cation, d-electrons of Pt(V), oxidant or fluorinating agent
summary: Oxygen gas meets the deep-red vapour of PtF6 and an orange-red ionic solid appears. Press start and the lab does the rest: an ionisation-energy scale shows why one electron jumps, oxidation numbers show who is reduced, the MO diagram of O2 fills and loses one pi* electron to give bond order 2.5, platinum is stripped to Pt(V) 5d5, and every fluorine atom is counted before each option is tested claim - evidence - verdict. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
subtopics: Bond order from MO electron configurations - O2, O2+, O2-, O2 2-
Paramagnetism and unpaired electrons in MO theory
Oxidation states and electron configuration of transition-metal ions (Pt 5d9 6s1)
Octahedral d-orbital splitting, low spin 5d ions
Oxidant versus fluorinating agent - Bartlett's O2+[PtF6]-
concepts: PtF6 has a very high electron affinity (about 7 eV) and takes one electron from O2 (IE 12.07 eV): O2 + PtF6 -> O2+[PtF6]-, so X+ = O2+ and Y- = [PtF6]-
O2+ has 15 electrons; the electron removed from O2 was antibonding (pi*2p), so bonding 10 and antibonding 5 give bond order 2.5 - not 1.5, which is superoxide O2-: (A) false
In [PtF6]- platinum is +5; Pt [Xe]4f14 5d9 6s1 loses 6s1 and four 5d electrons, leaving 5d5 (t2g5): (B) true
Pt goes from +6 in PtF6 to +5 in [PtF6]-: PtF6 is reduced, so it is the oxidant: (C) true
All six F atoms stay on Pt and no O-F bond forms - no fluorine is transferred, so PtF6 is not acting as a fluorinating agent: (D) false
Bartlett noticed IE(Xe) 12.13 eV is almost the same as IE(O2) and made the first noble-gas compound the same year
formulas: O2+: sigma1s2 sigma*1s2 sigma2s2 sigma*2s2 sigma2pz2 pi2px2 pi2py2 pi*2px1 -> (10 - 5)/2 = 2.5

derivedQuantities.custom_NO: NO+[PtF6]-, bond order 3.0 - not the question's compound

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: X+ = O2+, Y- = [PtF6]-; bond order 2.5; Pt(V) 5d5; PtF6 the oxidant, not a fluorinating agent; (B), (C)
Mass and charge balance: the only +1/-1 split of O2PtF6 that keeps a hexafluoro anion is O2+[PtF6]-; every other split needs an O-F bond

Molecular-orbital filling written independently of the page (aufbau + Hund): O2 2- 1, O2- 1.5, O2 2, O2+ 2.5, N2 3, NO+ 3; the sigma2p/pi2p ordering changes no bond order; measured bond lengths 149 > 133 > 121 > 112 pm follow the same order
Hartree-Fock (pyscf UHF/6-31G*): equilibrium bond O2+ 1.07 < O2 1.17 < O2- 1.30 A and Mayer bond order 2.26 > 1.83 > 1.38
Oxidation states by charge balance (sympy): Pt +6 in PtF6, +5 in [PtF6]-; Pt [Xe]4f14 5d9 6s1 -> 5d5 (t2g5, one unpaired)
Electron and fluorine ledger: O2 loses 1, Pt gains 1; F on Pt 6 -> 6, F on O 0
Independent script tests/verify_p1q07.py: 27 of 27 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q39) gives (B), (C) with the same reasoning

verification.note: Built with the PrayogX next-question skill. The ~12.2 eV oxidising limit of PtF6 is shown as Bartlett's empirical observation (O2 12.07 and Xe 12.13 eV react, N2 15.58 eV does not), not as a computed threshold.

interactivity: Mission brief with X+ = ?, Y- = ? and Pt oxidation state = ? tiles that fill in as the lab finds them

Station 1: a reaction bulb of deep-red PtF6 vapour, O2 flowing in, sparks where an electron jumps and an orange-red solid settling; an ionisation-energy scale with the PtF6 window (NO, O2, Xe, N2) and the electron travelling from gas to PtF6
Station 2: oxidation-number bookkeeping - O2 oxidised, Pt +6 -> +5 reduced - PtF6 is the oxidant

Station 3: the MO diagram of O2 filling electron by electron (Hund's rule), the pi* electron leaving, live bonding / antibonding counts, then the bond-order ladder of the O2 family with measured bond lengths

Station 4: platinum's 5d and 6s boxes stripped to Pt(+6) and given the electron back to Pt(+5); octahedral [PtF6]- in 3D with t2g/eg filling; a fluorine audit before and after, with ClF3 + U as the contrast of real fluorination
